alt: Your best-selling product could be hiding a weak margin.
Best seller is not best profit: High sales - Feels like winning.; Many costs - Delivery, fees, ads, returns.; Small profit - What is left is what counts.
Revenue is not profit. Revenue is what customers pay. Profit is what stays after every cost of selling that product.
Subtract in order: Product cost - What you pay for it.; Selling costs - Delivery, fees, packaging.; Marketing and returns - Ad cost and return losses.
Hypothetical figures. One order, step by step: Selling price $30; Product cost -$14; Delivery you pay -$3; Fees and packaging -$2; Ad cost per order -$6; Profit per order $5
Two numbers, two stories. Product margin only: $30 price, $14 cost; About 53%. Looks great.. After all costs: $5 profit per order; About 17% of the price.

caption:
Your best-selling product could be hiding a weak margin. 💡

Revenue is what customers pay. Profit is what is left after the product, delivery, payment fees, packaging, ads and returns.

In our hypothetical example, a $30 product with a $14 cost looks like a 53% margin. After delivery ($3), payment fees and packaging ($2) and ads ($6), the profit is $5 per order, about 17% of the price. These are sample figures only, so use your own numbers.
